notes.body: assigned to @martin.r.mathieson
@oakimk - there were some length fields recently changed to unsigned types, but were still (harmlessly, but confusingly) testing with \<= 0
:( which Werror did you enable to show these? It doesn't look good and should not happen again!

I'm not sure if there is compiler warning that would catch them, I've seen them reported by cppcheck (it gets called at the end of check_dissector.py, and somehow has lurched into life a month after we stopped getting coverity updates..)
To be clear, I haven't seen any cases where your changes have caused a problem by changing length fields from unsigned to signed, but we do need to be careful if they are used in a loop guard.

added 1 commit
  • 87e87eb7 - dissectors: address more cppcheck warnings
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25442/diffs?diff_id=1857388083&start_sha=6cbf406d9bb4494e255fce980753ea43e53ab1de)

Sometimes there can be infinite loops changing the length fields to unsigned, if the code previously depended on overflow subtracting a length, and a field was not actually added in a way that would have thrown an exception. Hopefully we will see fuzz errors if that happens.

Yes, I was warning Joakim to be careful about this with the changes he has been working on.

As I noted in another comment, I'm not sure about the variable I touched in packet-bthci_cmd.c

The one in packet-btle.c is ok - it gets re-read on each loop..
Should this become unsigned too?
It probably should.  I was only addressing the fact that the 0 definitely gets overwritten.
